thread.title: Dow tumbles 160 points in early Tuesday trade as rebound attempt sputters - MarketWatch

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Dow tumbles 160 points in early Tuesday trade as rebound attempt sputters - MarketWatch
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average traded more than 100 points lower Tuesday morning, as a tumble in shares of Boeing Co. BA, -3.90% and Home Depot Inc. HD, -2.94% put the kibosh on a rebound attempt by the blue-chip index. Boeing's share decline was carving about 80 points out of the Dow DJIA, -0.52% after The Wall Street Journal reported that the aerospace company withheld information about a change to its aircrafts, while Home Depot was retreating even after the home-improvement giant reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. Declines in both companies come after the Dow shed more than 600 points amid a internet and technology-related stock-market rout that was partly prompted by sharp declines in shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.15% and those for Goldman Sachs Group Inc. GS, -0.27% Most recently, the Dow was trading 160 points, or 0.6%, lower at 25,210, the S&P 500 index SPX, +0.00% was down 0.2% at 2,721, while the Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +0.41% was clinging to a slight 0.1% gain at 7,210. All three benchmarks finished Monday's trade sharply lower.
